alt: Four rows: A listening (interpret what images add to spoken text), B reading (treat layout, images and formatting as meaning), C speaking (interact spontaneously and answer what was asked) and D writing (match register, vocabulary and structure to audience and purpose). All are judged against the student’s own proficiency level.
caption: Each criterion rewards a skill beyond literal comprehension or rehearsed language.

after: ## Where this fits in the subject
alt: Three columns of rising height for the emergent, capable and proficient levels. Top-band evidence at the emergent level can be a short, simple but accurate response with basic vocabulary; at the proficient level it needs nuanced, extended, spontaneous language. Judge your work against your own level’s descriptors.
caption: The same response can be top band at one level and mid band at a higher one.

alt: A spoken announcement about a temporary closure is played with an image of a closed sign. A lower response only identifies facts heard, such as time and place; a top-band response also explains how the closed-sign image reinforces the spoken message.
caption: Top-band listening explains how the visuals support or add to what is said.

alt: A schematic public information poster with a red warning banner, short text and colour-coded icons. Top-band reading comprehends the written text and also explains what the icons and colours communicate, such as a red icon signalling urgency or warning. Treating the visuals as decoration is not top band.
caption: Read the layout, icons and colours as part of the message.

alt: An examiner asks an unexpected follow-up question. Falling back on a memorised, unrelated prepared answer cannot show top-band criterion C. A top-band response answers the actual question directly and coherently, with a range of vocabulary and structures suited to the level.
caption: Spontaneous, relevant interaction beats a rehearsed speech.

alt: A text message to a friend uses informal, abbreviated language, while a formal email to a school administrator on a related topic uses a formal greeting and sign-off, complete sentences and polite requests. Writing the same content with only the greeting changed is not top band.
caption: Top-band writing changes register, vocabulary and structure, not just the greeting.
